partners.mechanism_chain: PIK3R1 (HGNC:9523) —DISRUPTS→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74) —LEADS_TO→ Adrenal hyperplasia (HP:0005932); RET (HGNC:9997) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74) —LEADS_TO→ Medullary thyroid carcinoma (HP:0005842); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP74) —LEADS_TO→ Pheochromocytoma (HP:0005921). Loss-of-function mutations in PIK3R1 lead to haploinsufficiency and disruption of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, causing SHORT syndrome with phenotypes such as short stature and adrenal hyperplasia. Gain-of-function mutations in RET, the primary driver of MEN2A, also lead to the activation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, contributing to the development of medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma.
